title: Cognitive Behavioral Counseling with Cognitive Restructuring Techniques to Improve Academic Resilience in Junior High School Students
text_snippet: Cognitive Behavioral Counseling with Cognitive Restructuring Techniques to Improve Academic Resilience in Junior High School Students Many junior high school students experience academic pressure that affects their mental resilience and ability to face learning challenges. This low level of academic resilience indicates the need for structured counseling interventions, such as cognitive behavioral counseling using cognitive restructuring techniques. Therefore, the aim of this study is to examine the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral counseling with cognitive restructuring techniques in improving the academic resilience of junior high school students. This research employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design of the non-equivalent pretest-posttest control group type. The research subjects consisted of 16 eighth-grade students with low academic resilience, selected through purposive sampling and divided into experimental and control groups. Data were collected using an academic resilience scale questionnaire developed based on the seven aspects by Reivich and Shatté, and were quantitatively analyzed using an independent sample t-test with the assistance of SPSS 25. title: Cognitive Behavioral Counseling Guide Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques to Reduce Academic Anxiety in Students
text_snippet: Cognitive Behavioral Counseling Guide Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques to Reduce Academic Anxiety in Students Cognitive behavioral counseling is one of the approaches that has been proven effective in addressing various psychological problems among students. However, the high level of academic anxiety among secondary school students has not been optimally addressed through guidance and counseling services. This study aims to develop and examine the effectiveness of a cognitive behavioral counseling guidebook with cognitive restructuring techniques in reducing academic anxiety. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the 4-D model, which consists of the define, design, develop, and disseminate stages. The research subjects included six students with high levels of academic anxiety as the effectiveness testing sample and six expert validators consisting of lecturers and guidance and counseling practitioners. Data were collected using an academic anxiety questionnaire through a pretest–posttest design. Data analysis was conducted using content validity tests (CVR and CVI), reliability testing (Cronbach’s Alpha), prerequisite tests (normality and homogeneity), hypothesis testing using the Paired Sample T-Test, and effect size analysis using Cohen’s D. title: The Implementation of Problem-Based Learning to Overcome Communication Barriers in Public Speaking in the Counseling Process
text_snippet: The Implementation of Problem-Based Learning to Overcome Communication Barriers in Public Speaking in the Counseling Process Communication and public speaking skills are essential for counselors to establish effective therapeutic relationships. However, communication barriers often reduce the quality of counseling. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of Problem-Based Learning (PBL) in improving communication skills, particularly public speaking in counseling contexts. This study employed a systematic literature review method with a descriptive qualitative approach based on the PRISMA framework. The research subjects consisted of 32 scientific articles that met the inclusion criteria from the period 2015–2024, obtained through searches in five major electronic databases. Data collection was conducted using a structured data extraction form that had been validated with an inter-rater reliability of 0.847. Data analysis was carried out through thematic analysis combined with qualitative content analysis using six systematic stages. title: Fear of Missing Out with Problematic Smartphone Use in Adolescents
text_snippet: Fear of Missing Out with Problematic Smartphone Use in Adolescents The development of information technology allows individuals to access various information easily. However, smartphone use can become problematic when individuals are unable to control their usage. Problematic smartphone use refers to a condition in which a person cannot regulate smartphone use, resulting in negative impacts on daily life. This study aimed to analyze the relationship between fear of missing out and problematic smartphone use among adolescents. The study employed a quantitative approach with a sample of 255 adolescents obtained through convenience sampling. Data were collected using two instruments, namely the Problematic Mobile Phone Use Scale (PMPUS) and the Online Fear of Missing Out Scale (On-FoMO), and analyzed using Pearson correlation. The results showed a significant positive relationship between fear of missing out and problematic smartphone use (r = 0.705; p = 0.000). In conclusion, fear of missing out is an important factor influencing excessive smartphone use among adolescents. The implication is that these findings can serve as a basis for developing prevention strategies and interventions to help adolescents manage smartphone use more healthily.

title: Aiken’s Index Analysis to Determine the Content Validity of the Self-Adjustment Instrument Based on Schneider’s Theory
text_snippet: Aiken’s Index Analysis to Determine the Content Validity of the Self-Adjustment Instrument Based on Schneider’s Theory New students in Islamic boarding schools often face challenges in the process of adjusting due to environmental changes that include social, academic, and religious dimensions. Inability to adapt can have a negative impact on their mental health and educational success. This study aims to develop and test the content validity of an adjustment instrument for new students, which is based on Schneiders' theory (1964). The method used is quantitative descriptive with a focus on the analysis of the content validity of the instrument. The research subjects involved three experts in the fields of psychology, guidance counseling, and assessment. Data were collected through expert assessment of 32 statement items representing eight indicators of four main aspects of adjustment. Content validity was analyzed using the Aiken's V technique to assess the suitability of indicators, content relevance, and clarity of wording. The results of the analysis showed that 25 of the 32 items obtained an Aiken index between 0.92 and 1.00 indicating high content validity, while the other seven items obtained a value of 0.83 and were recommended for revision. title: Adolescent Mental Health from the Perspective of Ki Hadjar Dewantara
text_snippet: Adolescent Mental Health from the Perspective of Ki Hadjar Dewantara The background of this research was based on the rising prevalence of mental disorders among adolescents, triggered by academic pressure, social dynamics, family environment, and the influence of the digital world. A qualitative approach was used, employing a literature study method. This study aimed to examine the issue of adolescent mental health through the philosophical approach of Ki Hadjar Dewantara’s educational thought. Data were obtained from various scholarly documents and relevant literature sources, then analyzed descriptively with an emphasis on Ki Hadjar Dewantara’s conceptual framework, particularly the Tri-Center of Education, the Trilogy of Education, and the concept of the School as a Garden. The results indicated that adolescent mental health is strongly influenced by the social environments that simultaneously shape them, namely the family, school, and community. Schools, as formal educational spaces, play a crucial role in maintaining students' mental balance. When schools fail to provide an emotionally supportive atmosphere, adolescents become increasingly vulnerable to mental health problems. title: Instructions for Administering Spector’s Work Locus of Control Scale (WLCS) as a Measure of Beliefs among Contract Teachers
text_snippet: Instructions for Administering Spector’s Work Locus of Control Scale (WLCS) as a Measure of Beliefs among Contract Teachers The issue of honorary teachers remains a significant concern, particularly regarding their welfare and job performance, which are influenced by both internal and external factors. In this context, locus of control is an important variable in understanding how individuals perceive control over their work outcomes. This study aims to analyze the tendency of internal and external locus of control among honorary teachers using Spector’s Work Locus of Control Scale (WLCS). This research employed a quantitative approach with a descriptive design, involving 27 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a 16-item WLCS questionnaire measuring internal and external dimensions. Descriptive statistical analysis revealed that the majority of respondents tended toward an internal locus of control (65%), while the remaining respondents showed an external tendency (35%). In addition, perceptions of external factors exhibited greater variability compared to internal factors. title: 21st Century Career Trends: A Study on Career Preferences and Needs of Generation Z
text_snippet: 21st Century Career Trends: A Study on Career Preferences and Needs of Generation Z The development of technology and the dynamics of the 21st-century workforce demand adaptive career readiness, however, many Generation Z students still lack a clear sense of career direction. This study aims to analyze the career preferences and needs of Generation Z and to explore dominant career trends based on the results of the Rothwell-Miller Interest Blank (RMIB) assessment. The research employs a descriptive approach with a cross-sectional survey design. The study involved 77 students from the 2024 cohort, selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using the RMIB test instrument, which measures 12 categories of career interests, and were then analyzed descriptively using quantitative percentages of interest tendencies. The results indicate that the three fields with the highest levels of interest are social skills (80%), medical (66%), and clerical (64%). These findings suggest that Generation Z tends to prioritize careers that are socially meaningful, involve interpersonal interaction, provide stability, and offer opportunities for personal development. title: Forgiveness Therapy: A Tool for Managing Female Victims of Spousal Battery
text_snippet: Forgiveness Therapy: A Tool for Managing Female Victims of Spousal Battery Marriage is fundamentally regarded as a social institution that is expected to provide emotional security, support, and psychological well-being for individuals. However, in reality, not all marital relationships function as expected, as domestic violence remains a prevalent issue that significantly affects victims, particularly women. Such violence often results in prolonged trauma, diminished self-worth, and complex emotional distress. This study aims to analyze the role of forgiveness therapy as a counseling intervention in managing trauma among female victims of domestic violence. The study employs a conceptual research design using a systematic literature review of relevant scholarly sources. Data were collected through the analysis of journal articles, academic books, and empirical findings in the fields of psychology and counseling, and were analyzed using qualitative descriptive techniques. The analysis focuses on the application of Enright’s four-phase forgiveness therapy model, which includes the uncovering, decision, work, and outcome phases. title: Behavioral Counseling with Modeling Techniques to Improve Seventh-Grade Students’ Self-Confidence
text_snippet: Behavioral Counseling with Modeling Techniques to Improve Seventh-Grade Students’ Self-Confidence Low self-confidence among students is a significant issue affecting both academic achievement and social interactions. Prior to the intervention, 66.5% of seventh grade students demonstrated low levels of self-confidence. This study aims to simultaneously analyze the effectiveness of behavioral counseling using the modeling technique in enhancing students’ self-confidence. The research employed a quasi experimental design with a Nonequivalent Pretest-Posttest Control Group. The subjects were seventh-grade students, divided into an experimental group (34 students) and a control group (34 students) through random sampling. Data were collected using a questionnaire developed based on Peter Lauster’s theory and analyzed descriptively, with N-Gain used to measure improvement. Results indicated that 91.2% of students in the experimental group reached high to very high self-confidence levels, whereas the control group showed only limited improvement. The study concludes that behavioral counseling with the modeling technique effectively enhances students’ self-confidence and promotes active participation in learning. title: Development of a Creative Personality Instrument for University Students: An Analysis of Validity and Reliability
text_snippet: Development of a Creative Personality Instrument for University Students: An Analysis of Validity and Reliability The availability of instruments to identify students’ creative personality based on positive psychology remains limited. Furthermore, the integration of the creativity paradox concept in existing instruments is not yet optimal. The study aims to develop and evaluate a Creative Personality instrument grounded in Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi’s theory of creativity paradox, which encompasses ten pairs of paradoxical characteristics within the academic context. This research employed a mixed methods approach with a sequential exploratory design. The participants consisted of 115 students aged 18–25 years. Data were collected through literature review, expert discussions, and questionnaires. Content validity was assessed through expert judgment, while empirical validity was analyzed using Pearson Product Moment correlation, and reliability was tested using Cronbach’s Alpha coefficient. The findings indicate that most instrument items met the validity criteria and demonstrated a very high level of reliability, suggesting that the instrument is appropriate for use. title: Impact of Financial Stress on Marital Relationships of Married Adults in Kwara State, Nigeria
text_snippet: Impact of Financial Stress on Marital Relationships of Married Adults in Kwara State, Nigeria Financial stress marked by economic hardship, unstable income, debt, and unmet basic needs has become a common challenge amid Nigeria’s fluctuating economy. This study examines its impact on marital relationships among married adults in Kwara State.The population consisted of all married adults in Kwara state. Simple random sampling techniques was employed to select 200 married adults across Kwara state. The instrument used for data collection was entitled ‘‘Financial Stress and Marital Relationships Questionnaire’’ (FSMRQ). One research question was raised while three (3) hypotheses were formulated and tested at 0.05 level of significance. The data obtained were analyzed using t-test and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The results show that married adults in Kwara state faced communication breakdown and also discovered changes in partners behaviour. Findings of the study also revealed that there was no significant difference in the impact of financial stress on marital relationships among married adults based on gender, age, marital status and educational background. title: Evaluation of Group Counseling Based on REBT in Reducing People-Pleasing Tendencies Among University Students

Group guidance interventions can help transform irrational cognitive, emotional, and behavioral patterns into more rational ones. This study aims to empirically evaluate the effectiveness of group counseling services based on Rational Emotive Behavior Therapy (REBT) in reducing people-pleasing attitudes among students. The method used is quantitative research with a pre-experimental design in the form of a one-group pre-test post-test. The research population consists of 82 students, with a sample of 10 students selected through simple random sampling techniques. The data collection instrument is a Likert scale questionnaire administered before and after the group counseling service. Data analysis techniques include normality tests, homogeneity tests, and hypothesis testing using the sign test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The results of the study indicate a significant decrease in people-pleasing attitudes after the intervention. title: Effectiveness of Behavioral Counseling Theory Using Behavior Contract Techniques to Reduce Academic Procrastination in Middle School Students
text_snippet: Effectiveness of Behavioral Counseling Theory Using Behavior Contract Techniques to Reduce Academic Procrastination in Middle School Students Academic procrastination is the deliberate postponement of academic tasks to the next day, often by engaging in other activities that are more enjoyable to the individual, which consumes a significant amount of time needed to complete the tasks. Academic procrastination can lead to poor time management. The purpose of this study was to analyze the effectiveness of behavioral counseling theory using behavior contract techniques in reducing academic procrastination among middle school students. This study employed a quantitative method with a quasi-experimental design, using a nonequivalent pre-test and post-test control group approach. The subjects involved in this study were 50 middle school students. Data collection methods included documentation and questionnaires, followed by statistical analysis consisting of prerequisite tests and hypothesis testing. Based on the data analysis, the results showed that the behavior contract technique was effective in reducing academic procrastination among 8th-grade students, as evidenced by their pre-test and post-test scores. title: Effectiveness of Behavioral Counseling Using Self-Management Techniques to Reduce Online Game Addiction in Junior High School Students
text_snippet: Effectiveness of Behavioral Counseling Using Self-Management Techniques to Reduce Online Game Addiction in Junior High School Students Online game addiction affects students’ academic productivity. Many students fail to complete assignments given by teachers because they spend more time playing online games than studying. Some students even arrive late to school due to oversleeping after staying up late playing online games at night. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of behavioral counseling using self-management techniques in reducing online game addiction among eighth-grade junior high school students. This research is a quasi-experimental study with a nonequivalent pre-test and post-test control group design. The subjects involved were eighth-grade students, divided into one control group and one experimental group, totaling 50 students selected based on criteria for online game addiction. Data collection methods included document recording and questionnaires. The data were then analyzed using statistical analysis, consisting of prerequisite tests and hypothesis testing. Based on the data analysis, the results indicate that behavioral counseling using self-management techniques is effective in reducing online game addiction among students.

title: Guidebook Based on Behavioral Counseling with Modeling Technique to Improve Students’ Self-Confidence
text_snippet: Guidebook Based on Behavioral Counseling with Modeling Technique to Improve Students’ Self-Confidence Students’ self-confidence varies; some students feel very confident, while others experience low self-confidence. In line with this, this study aims to develop a guidebook based on behavioral counseling using the modeling technique to improve students’ self-confidence. This study applied a Research and Development approach using the 4D model. Data analysis was conducted using the Content Validity Ratio method involving five experts in the field of guidance and counseling as validation subjects. The practicality test involved 10 guidance and counseling teachers, and the effectiveness test was conducted on 10 students. The validation results showed that the developed guidebook obtained a content validation score and a Content Validity Index value of 1, indicating that the guidebook has very high content validity. title: The Effectiveness of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy in Reducing Anxiety in Women Victims of Domestic Violence
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy in Reducing Anxiety in Women Victims of Domestic Violence The study is motivated by the anxiety and guilt experienced by women victims of domestic violence, which arise from attempts to reject negative thoughts after experiencing abuse. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is predicted to reduce such anxiety and help individuals coexist with painful experiences rather than fight or try to eliminate them. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy in reducing anxiety in women victims of domestic violence (DV). The research employed a one-group pretest-posttest design. The sample consisted of five women victims of DV. Anxiety was measured using the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scale, and data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon Rank test. The results indicated that ACT is effective in reducing anxiety among women victims of DV, with a p-value of 0.048

title: The Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Counseling Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques in a Group Counseling Setting to Address Academic Anxiety in Vocational High School Students
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Counseling Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques in a Group Counseling Setting to Address Academic Anxiety in Vocational High School Students The learning process of students is influenced by both internal and external factors, including academic anxiety arising from cognitive distortions. This anxiety can disrupt concentration, lower academic performance, and trigger maladaptive behaviors. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of cognitive-behavioral counseling using cognitive restructuring techniques on 11th-grade vocational high school (SMK) students. Observations revealed that several students experienced academic anxiety with somatic, emotional, cognitive, and behavioral symptoms, often linked to negative experiences such as exam-related trauma. Individual counseling provided by the school guidance counselor (BK) was found to be insufficient, highlighting the need for group counseling using cognitive restructuring techniques. The study employed a true experimental design with a pre-test/post-test control group design, involving 34 students divided into experimental and control groups. Data were collected using a Likert-scale academic anxiety questionnaire and analyzed with a paired-sample t-test. title: A Brief Solution-Focused Counseling Guide to Improve Self-Regulated Learning in Vocational High School Students
text_snippet: A Brief Solution-Focused Counseling Guide to Improve Self-Regulated Learning in Vocational High School Students The low level of self regulated learning among vocational high school students, reflected in the lack of learning initiative, delays in task completion, and limited self-reflection ability due to both internal and external factors, becomes an obstacle in achieving an optimal learning process. This study aims to develop and test the effectiveness of a Solution-Focused Brief Counseling (SFBC) guidebook in improving students’ self-regulated learning. The research employed a research and development design followed by a pretest-posttest control group experiment. The research subjects consisted of 24 students who were randomly assigned into a control group (N=12) and an experimental group (N=12). The data collection instrument was a validated self-regulated learning scale, with data analysis using the Shapiro-Wilk test for normality and the Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test (Mann-Whitney U-Test) to examine differences between groups. title: The Meaning of Life for Balinese Women: A Phenomenological Study in Balinese Society
text_snippet: The Meaning of Life for Balinese Women: A Phenomenological Study in Balinese Society Balu woman in Balinese culture are single mother due to the death of her husband. This event generates negative perceptions, emotional distress, and added burdens from traditional regulations (awig-awig). Despite these challenges, balu women eventually find new positive meaning in life. However, research on how this transformation occurs remains limited. This study aims to explore how balu women construct the meaning of life after two years of living with this role. This research uses a qualitative phenomenological approach with Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), data were collected through semi-structured interviews with three subjects. The results of the study show that there are different meanings of life before, after, and two years of living as a balu woman. In the initial phase, the balu woman had a positive perception of their lives, but after taking on the status of a balu woman, negative perceptions emerged due to problems and emotional shocks experienced. title: The Relationship between Sense of School Belonging and Acts of Vandalism among Students by Gender
text_snippet: The Relationship between Sense of School Belonging and Acts of Vandalism among Students by Gender Vandalism is a serious issue in schools. However, previous research has limited information on how this relates to a sense of school belonging among both male and female students. To address this gap, this study aims to analyze the relationship between sense of school belonging and vandalism among students, based on gender. This study employed a quantitative, correlational approach involving 84 high school students. Data were collected using an 18-item sense of school belonging scale and a 21-item vandalism questionnaire, with satisfactory validity and Cronbach's Alpha values of .915 and .961, respectively. Data were analyzed using product moment and independent sample t-tests. The results showed a significant, negative relationship between sense of school belonging and vandalism among high school students. Male students had a lower average score (mean = 39.45) compared to female students (mean = 56.07) for sense of school belonging, and vice versa for vandalism (male Mean = 53.03 and female Mean = 37.59). These findings reveal a significant difference in terms of student gender. The implications of this study provide insights for educators and policy makers in school institutions

title: Positive Self-Talk among Senior High School Students: A Descriptive Quantitative Study
text_snippet: Positive Self-Talk among Senior High School Students: A Descriptive Quantitative Study Adolescents in secondary schools begin to face various challenges and social demands that can trigger negative emotions such as guilt, shame, and social withdrawal. This condition requires the ability to manage thoughts and emotions in a healthy way. One effective psychological strategy is positive self-talk, a form of positive thinking that can enhance psychological well-being. Low levels of positive self-talk may negatively affect adolescents’ mental health. This study aimed to determine the level of positive self-talk among high school students in Kupang City. The research employed a quantitative descriptive method with a cross-sectional survey design. A total of 342 high school students were selected as participants using simple random sampling. Data were collected using a psychological scale instrument, specifically the Self-Talk Scale, and analyzed using IBM SPSS software through descriptive statistical analysis. The results showed that, in general, the positive self-talk level of high school students was in the moderate category. title: The Use of Brain Teaser Game Media in Information Services to Develop Students' Critical Reasoning Skills

However, field observations indicate that the critical reasoning skills of twelfth-grade students remain low. However, in practice, many students still demonstrate low learning responsibility, which, if left unaddressed, can negatively affect their academic achievement. Therefore, guidance and counseling services serve as a strategic means to foster students’ sense of responsibility in the academic context. This research employs a quasi-experimental approach with a nonequivalent pretest-posttest control group design. title: The Role of Educational Psychology in Preventing Deviant Behavior in Schools
text_snippet: The Role of Educational Psychology in Preventing Deviant Behavior in Schools Deviant behavior among students is a serious issue that can hinder both the educational process and the development of adolescents’ personalities. This condition requires systematic intervention through the role of Guidance and Counseling (GC) teachers who not only provide services but also create a conducive educational climate. This study aims to analyze the role of educational psychology in preventing students’ deviant behavior through guidance and counseling strategies. A qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through in-depth interviews and documentation. The research subjects consisted of one coordinator of GC teachers and two active GC teachers. Data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and thematic conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that GC teachers play a strategic role in preventing deviant behavior through individual and group counseling, which effectively enhances students’ awareness, discipline, and responsibility. text_snippet: Academic Flow in Vocational High School Students in Relatin to Self-Efficacy and Self-Regulated Learning This study is motivated by low learning motivation, students’ lack of focus in following classroom instruction, and the suboptimal completion of school assignments. The purpose of this study is to analyze the simultaneous relationship between self-regulated learning and self-efficacy on academic flow. This study employs a quantitative approach with a correlational method. The research sample consisted of 218 vocational high school students. Data were collected using a Likert scale, with instruments including the academic flow scale, self-regulated learning scale, and self-efficacy scale. title: Behavioral Counseling with Self-Management Techniques to Minimize Academic Procrastination Behavior in Junior High School Students
text_snippet: Behavioral Counseling with Self-Management Techniques to Minimize Academic Procrastination Behavior in Junior High School Students Academic procrastination is one of the common problems experienced by adolescents, which negatively impacts both academic achievement and mental health. Limited self-regulation ability is a dominant factor that causes students to delay completing tasks. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of self-management techniques in reducing academic procrastination among students. The research employed a quasi-experimental design with a quantitative approach, specifically a non-equivalent control group design. The research subjects consisted of 16 students selected through purposive sampling based on high levels of academic procrastination, and they were divided into an experimental group and a control group, each comprising 8 students. The instruments used in this study included observation, interviews, and an academic procrastination questionnaire based on a Likert scale. Data were analyzed using the Shapiro Wilk normality test, Levene’s test for homogeneity, and an independent sample t-test with the assistance of SPSS 22 software. title: Measuring Students’ Comfort and Happiness in Learning Science: Non-Test Assesment Instruments for Grade V Elementary School
text_snippet: Measuring Students’ Comfort and Happiness in Learning Science: Non-Test Assesment Instruments for Grade V Elementary School The reality of elementary education indicates a gap in providing a learning environment that supports students’ psychological aspects. Many schools have not been able to create a comfortable and joyful learning atmosphere, especially in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) learning, which requires the integration of multiple disciplines. This study aims to analyze, develop, and evaluate a non-test assessment instrument book consisting of observation sheets, questionnaires, and interview guidelines to measure students’ comfort and happiness in learning. This research employed a descriptive quantitative design using the ADDIE development model, which includes Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages. The subjects involved one assessment instrument book as the developed product, with input from media experts, instrument experts, teachers, and students as respondents. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and questionnaires, and analyzed quantitatively using validity indices and response percentages. title: Increasing Multicultural Awareness: Guidance and Counseling Practices of Teachers in Bogor City
text_snippet: Increasing Multicultural Awareness: Guidance and Counseling Practices of Teachers in Bogor City Cultural diversity in schools requires guidance and counseling (GC) teachers to possess multicultural awareness and the ability to integrate it into student services. However, the implementation of multicultural counseling practices remains suboptimal due to limited training and professional development. This study aims to analyze GC teachers’ understanding of multicultural awareness and to explore its implementation in counseling practices. A qualitative approach with a case study design was employed. The research involved 12 GC teachers selected purposively. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and document analysis, with the researcher as the main instrument. Data validity was ensured through triangulation, prolonged engagement, and expert discussions. Thematic analysis was applied to interpret the findings. The results reveal that GC teachers demonstrate adequate understanding of multicultural awareness; however, its application in planning, implementation, and evaluation stages of counseling services remains partial and inconsistent. title: Implementation of Asung Luwan Folktale Media to Strengthening Students' Cultural Awareness
text_snippet: Implementation of Asung Luwan Folktale Media to Strengthening Students' Cultural Awareness Folktales spread throughout the Indonesian archipelago are seen as having the potential to explore local culture. Local wisdom is one of the cultural products. These cultural products can be used as references for social life and communication, both communication with other humans, nature, and God. Cultural issues such as stereotypes, discrimination, and microaggressions are prone to occur in intercultural interactions, especially in Indonesia, where every citizen has a diverse cultural background. The purpose of this study is to increase students' cultural awareness through group guidance services using the Aung Luwan Folktale as the medium. The research method used is Guidance and Counseling Action Research (PTBK) with a qualitative descriptive approach. This activity involved 9 students from grade XI. Data collection techniques used were observation and interviews. The results of the research that has been conducted indicate that through group guidance services using the Asung Luwan folktale as the medium, students' cultural awareness can be increased. title: Strategies to Strengthening Bystander Critical Thinking through Educational Games: A Systematic Literature Review from a Technological Literacy Perspective
text_snippet: Strategies to Strengthening Bystander Critical Thinking through Educational Games: A Systematic Literature Review from a Technological Literacy Perspective Critical thinking skills and the active role of bystanders are essential competencies in shaping a generation that is responsive to social challenges in the digital era. However, in reality, many students remain passive as bystanders when witnessing bullying at school (das sein), even though they are expected to be critical and courageous enough to act (das sollen). This study aims to analyze strategies for strengthening bystanders’ critical thinking through educational games from a technological literacy perspective. This research is a systematic literature review (SLR) using the PRISMA approach. The subjects of the study consist of scientific articles published between 2020 and 2025, obtained through Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and ERIC. Data collection was carried out through document analysis, using a checklist instrument to assess article suitability. Data were analyzed using thematic synthesis on 10 selected articles. The main findings show that integrating educational games, technological literacy, and social interventions effectively improves students’ critical thinking skills, strengthens the role of active bystanders, and reduces passive behaviors. title: The Influence of Social Support and Hope on Grit among Final Year University Students
text_snippet: The Influence of Social Support and Hope on Grit among Final Year University Students Final year students often face psychological challenges such as pessimism, burnout, and low motivation when working on their thesis individually. These conditions lead to low levels of grit or perseverance in overcoming obstacles. This study aims to examine the effect of social support and hope on grit among final-year students. A descriptive quantitative approach with a survey method was employed. Data were collected through questionnaires using a purposive sampling technique involving 174 respondents. The research instruments included validated scales of social support, hope, and grit. Data analysis was conducted using multiple regression with SPSS version 25. title: The Influence of Self-Regulation and Time Management on Student Academic Procrastination
text_snippet: The Influence of Self-Regulation and Time Management on Student Academic Procrastination The problem in this study is academic procrastination that many students face and has a negative impact on academic achievement, where the main factors that play a role in reducing it are self-regulation, which helps students control behavior, emotions, and motivation, and time management, which allows students to organize and utilize time effectively. This study aims to analyze the relationship between self-regulation and time management on students' academic procrastination. This study used a quantitative approach with a correlational design and involved 95 students as samples. Data were collected through a scale of self-regulation, time management, and academic procrastination, then analyzed using descriptive test, normality test, and multiple linear regression. The results of the analysis showed that self-regulation and time management had a significant effect on academic procrastination with a value of F = 41.17 and R² = 0.581. title: Differences in Academic Insecurity Levels among Students Based on Gender
text_snippet: Differences in Academic Insecurity Levels among Students Based on Gender Academic insecurity is a psychological condition characterized by feelings of insecurity, fear of failure, anxiety, and a sense of incompetence in facing academic demands. The population in this study consisted of 577 sixth-semester students, with a sample of 212 students determined using purposive sampling based on Slovin’s formula. title: Inclusive-Counsel: Website-Based Inclusive Guidance and Counseling Service Design for Students with Special Needs
text_snippet: Inclusive-Counsel: Website-Based Inclusive Guidance and Counseling Service Design for Students with Special Needs The limited availability of assistant teachers with a background in special education presents a significant challenge in implementing inclusive education services. Guidance and counseling (GC) teachers play a crucial role as facilitators of psycho-pedagogical support for students with special needs (SEN). However, a lack of understanding of SEN characteristics and the absence of technical guidelines hinder the effectiveness of GC services. This study aims to design and develop an inclusive web-based digital GC service system to support SEN students in inclusive schools. The research employs a Design-Based Research (DBR) approach, consisting of two main phases: exploration and design. The exploration phase involved GC teachers as participants, with data collected through a readiness survey using a questionnaire, then analyzed using descriptive quantitative methods. Results show varied levels of teacher readiness to use digital services: 33.33% are categorized as ready, 38.89% as moderately ready, and 27.78% as less ready. title: Group Counseling Services Using the Creative Problem-Solving Technique to Reduce Students’ Academic Stress
text_snippet: Group Counseling Services Using the Creative Problem-Solving Technique to Reduce Students’ Academic Stress Academic stress is a psychological condition frequently experienced by students due to academic demands, performance expectations, and social pressures. If not addressed properly, this condition can negatively impact students’ mental health and academic performance. This study aims to determine the effectiveness of group counseling services using the Creative Problem-Solving (CPS) technique in reducing students’ academic stress.
